g.text: Qwen3-1.7B • released AWS F2 baseline • same visual conventions as the SimpleStories diagram
1,000 mapped DSP blocks = 648 projection + 336 attention + 16 normalization / rotary / elementwise
DSP blocks are FPGA arithmetic resources, not 1,000 independent multiplier lanes or an estimate of accessible training throughput.
1 Follow the data through the chip
Tokenization and display; token commands and replies; fixed-model upload at startup.
Loads the fixed model into HBM;
Owns operation order, layer, token position and internal tensor selection.
Embedding → 28 transformer layers → final normalization → vocabulary head → greedy token.
BF16 activations and K/V; specified FP32 work inside the engine.
Private tensor RAM; no host-visible intermediate-result port.
32 retained 64 KiB page slots in total.
Fixed root table; no secret auth key.
shared verifier; 128 UltraRAM blocks for payloads
Stores and fetches computed BF16 K/V.
Owns addresses, staging and valid prefix.
External K/V has NO integrity check
Fixed HBM port ownership + vendor memory controller
Model: ports 0–7. K/V payload: 8–15. Retained ports 16–23 are unused by this plain-K/V schedule.
External HBM — separate model and attention-cache regions
2.354 GB fixed model image, including tables/scales; mutable BF16 K/V. Neither is encrypted.
Used for Q/K/V, attention output, feed-forward projections and the tied vocabulary head.
A fixed selector chooses ONE bank per projection; these are not two concurrent matrix jobs.
Each box: 8 W8 × A16 products → 40-bit sum
Integer sum × computed vector scale × authenticated row scale.
324 mapped DSP blocks per bank, including accumulation and scaling
Each box: 8 W8 × A16 products → 40-bit sum
Integer sum × computed vector scale × authenticated row scale.
324 mapped DSP blocks per bank, including accumulation and scaling
Useful projection work: 256 products per accepted beat, not 512; stalls and other stages reduce average throughput.
One pair engine: two query heads share one K/V head. Reused across all eight K/V heads, in every layer.
Q and attention probabilities stay internal; K/V is fetched from the unprotected external cache.
Query head 0 of the current pair
Query head 1 of the current pair
Pink = runtime-operand arithmetic, not user-programmable arithmetic. Results return to private tensor memory.
Also present: fixed SiLU tables, activation quantization, adders, dividers and greedy argmax; not all use DSP blocks.
Floating-point multipliers may use multiple DSP blocks; integer adders can also map into DSP blocks.
Clocks in this image: 62.5 MHz inference / 125 MHz memory / 250 MHz host. 28 layers; hidden size 2,048; 16 Q heads / 8 K/V heads; head width 128.
HBM = high-bandwidth memory. BF16 / FP32 = floating-point formats. Private = no ordinary host operand/address interface, not physical memory secrecy.
Scope: selected paths in the released baseline, not every wire or a physical layout. 32,768-token design capacity is not full-context hardware qualification.
The AWS host and configuration plane are outside the inference-only claim. Mapped resources and a schematic do not prove physical-tamper resistance.
Sources: released Qwen RTL + HARDWARE.md + routed utilization-hierarchical.rpt; checkpoint 11d8d999… . Full identities and resource checks: companion inventory JSON.
